title: Conditions, Decisions and Boolean Logic

steps.title: Programs make decisions
steps.content: A condition is an expression that evaluates to true or false. An if statement runs its block only when its condition is true. The computer evaluates the condition first; it does not execute both branches.
steps.tip: Before tracing an if statement, calculate the condition's Boolean result.

steps.title: Read a comparison
steps.content: Comparison operators compare values and produce a Boolean result.
steps.prompt: If age is 17, what is the result of age >= 18?
steps.explanation: 17 is less than 18, so the comparison age >= 18 evaluates to false.
hints: Read the operator carefully: it includes equality as well as greater-than.
Compare the supplied value to the boundary without changing either value.

steps.title: Use if, elif and else
steps.content: Use if for the first condition, elif for another condition checked only when earlier conditions fail, and else for the remaining case. Order matters: the first true branch is the one that runs.
steps.tip: Place more specific or higher thresholds before broader fallback conditions.

steps.title: Trace the first matching branch
steps.content: Only one branch in this if/elif/else chain executes.
steps.prompt: What does this program print when score is 82?
steps.explanation: 82 >= 90 is false. The next test, 82 >= 75, is true, so B prints and the chain ends.
hints: Evaluate the first condition before reading the second.
The first true branch is selected; later branches in that chain are skipped.

steps.title: Combine conditions with and, or and not
steps.content: and is true only when both sides are true. or is true when at least one side is true. not reverses a Boolean value. Parentheses make compound conditions easier to read and prevent ambiguity.
steps.example:
has_id = True
age = 20
eligible = has_id and age >= 18
steps.tip: Break a compound condition into smaller true/false results before combining them.

steps.title: Evaluate a compound condition
steps.prompt: Let has_account = True and verified = False. What is has_account and verified?
steps.explanation: and requires both operands to be true. Since verified is false, the complete expression is false.
hints: Evaluate each side independently as true or false.
Only after that, apply the logical operator joining the two results.

steps.title: Trace a decision
steps.content: A decision is evaluated in a specific order: compute the condition, select the matching branch, and execute its body.
steps.prompt: Arrange the operations when an if statement is evaluated.
options: Skip the branch when the condition is false
steps.explanation: The condition is evaluated first. If it is false, that branch is skipped; if true, its body executes. The else branch is considered only when no earlier branch matches.
hints: A decision begins by evaluating its condition.
A false condition skips that branch body; a true condition enters it.

steps.title: Create an eligibility check
steps.content: Combine a numeric comparison with a Boolean flag. The output is a short decision message.
steps.prompt: Complete the condition so an account is approved only when both requirements are satisfied. Expected output: Approved.
hints: The age must be at least 18.
Both conditions must be true, so use the logical AND operator.
Use age >= 18 && identityVerified inside the if statement.

steps.title: Fix an incorrectly ordered grade check
steps.content: A student with 92 marks is receiving grade B because a broad condition runs before a more specific condition.
steps.prompt: Which change fixes the branch order?

feedback_by_option.1: The first condition already matches 92, so the later A condition is never checked. Test the higher threshold first.
feedback_by_option.2: Assignment or exact equality does not solve the ordering problem and would make the range logic incorrect.
feedback_by_option.3: The program needs conditional branching to choose a grade.
feedback_by_option.4: The issue is branch order, not the data type of score.

steps.explanation: The first true branch wins. Test the >= 90 case first, then the >= 75 fallback.
hints: Check whether the earlier, broader range can capture a value intended for the later, narrower range.
The most specific threshold should be tested before the fallback threshold.

questions.prompt: What must an if condition evaluate to for its body to run?
questions.explanation: The if body runs when its condition evaluates to true.

questions.prompt: If a = 5 and b = 8, what is the result of a < 10 and b > 6?
questions.explanation: 5 < 10 is true and 8 > 6 is true. true and true evaluates to true.

questions.prompt: In an if/elif/else chain, what happens after the first true branch executes?
options: The remaining branches in that chain are skipped
The if condition is evaluated again forever
questions.explanation: Only the first matching branch runs; later branches in the same chain are skipped.

questions.prompt: Which operator reverses a Boolean value in Python?
questions.explanation: not returns the opposite truth value. and and or combine Boolean expressions; == compares values.

questions.prompt: A discount is allowed only when a user is a member and the cart total is at least 1000. Which condition expresses this rule?
questions.explanation: Both requirements must hold, so combine membership and the threshold with and.

learning_objectives: Evaluate comparison expressions and identify their Boolean result.
Use if, elif and else to select one execution path.
Combine Boolean expressions using and, or and not.
Trace branch order and repair unreachable conditions.
Translate real eligibility rules into correct conditional logic.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Every branch in an if/elif/else chain is checked after one branch runs.
common_misconceptions.correction: Once the first true branch executes, the remaining branches in that chain are skipped.

common_misconceptions.misconception: and and or mean the same thing.
common_misconceptions.correction: and requires both sides to be true; or requires at least one side to be true.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Putting a broad threshold before a narrow threshold is harmless.
common_misconceptions.correction: The first true condition wins, so a broad branch can make a later specific branch unreachable.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A comparison such as score >= 40 changes score.
common_misconceptions.correction: A comparison produces a Boolean result; it does not assign a new value to score.

worked_examples.title: Choose a pass/fail branch
trace: Run the if body and assign Pass.
worked_examples.explanation: The condition decides which single branch runs.

worked_examples.title: Combine two requirements
worked_examples.input:
age = 19
has_id = True
allowed = age >= 18 and has_id
trace: Combine true and true with and.
worked_examples.explanation: A requirement joined with and is satisfied only when every part is true.

worked_examples.title: Fix unreachable branch logic
worked_examples.input:
if marks >= 40: pass
elif marks >= 80: pass
trace: The >= 80 condition is never reached for values 80 or above.
worked_examples.explanation: Specific thresholds should be tested before broader fallback conditions.

company_applications.practice: Trace nested branches and identify the exact printed output.
Translate multi-condition eligibility and grading rules into pseudocode.
Evaluate AND/OR statements and explain why a branch executes.
Find unreachable branches caused by incorrect condition order.

srs_cards.question: When does an if block execute?
srs_cards.answer: When its condition evaluates to true.

srs_cards.question: When is A and B true?
srs_cards.answer: Only when both A and B are true.

srs_cards.question: Why should high thresholds often appear before low thresholds in an if/elif grade chain?
srs_cards.answer: The first matching branch runs; a broad low threshold can prevent later high-threshold branches from ever being reached.

quest.story: The academy receives applications from learners with different scores and eligibility rules. It needs a reliable decision system that chooses exactly the correct route for each candidate.
quest.mission: Build and debug a set of decisions using comparisons, Boolean logic and correctly ordered branches.
success_criteria: Evaluate comparisons as true or false.
